thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High KV cache pressure detected on region-us-west-2 - p95 streaming latency spiked to 1.8s (baseline 120ms), p99 ~3.5s. Error budget burn alert triggered. Tagged as SEV3.
ashley: saw the alert, paging oncall now. linking dashboards: https://redwood.internal/d/kv-pressure/us-west-2
devin: i'm on it, pulling metrics from the prefill/decoder dashboard. initial impression: prefill miss rate jumped and decode queue depth increased.
mira: are customers seeing 5xx or just higher latency? any streaming stalls reported?
sam: customer-facing metrics show increase in streaming stalls for long-chat sessions (tokens >2048). Some sessions got stalled (~30s) then resumed. No widespread 5xx.
ashley: good to know. sounds like tail latency not hard error. can we confirm if eviction rates increased?
devin: eviction rate doubled in the last 3 minutes. KV slab utilization at 95%. Fragmentation index up from 0.12 to 0.42. Looks like prefill allocations are starving decode cold caches.
ashley: ok. hypothesis: prefill-heavy workload caused KV fragmentation + slab starvation, decode can't access prefetched KV -> decode stalls = streaming tail spikes.
mira: mitigations? we should consider throttling prefill or temporarily route heavy long sessions to fallback model with smaller KV working set.
sam: can we do an emergency routing rule to send sessions with estimated length >1500 tokens to model-generic-1 (lower KV footprint) for 10min?
alex: I can flip a routing rule in the runtime for us. prepping command. will notify when done.
ashley: also consider increasing 'slab_shrink_threshold' to free some pages? But that's risky mid-traffic.
devin: safer immediate step: reduce prefill concurrency by adjusting prefill.max_concurrent per hostpool from 8 -> 2. that should reduce new prefill allocations. command I propose: 
```
# runtimectl (prod) adjust prefill concurrency
runtimectl set hostpool us-west-2 prefill.max_concurrent=2 --reason "emergency kv pressure mitigation"
```
lia: +1 on lowering prefill concurrency. that will slow new long sessions starting but should let decode catch up.
ashley: alex, after routing change and devin's concurrency flip, we should watch p95/p99 and streaming stall rate for 5min. ready to execute?
alex: routing change applied: sessions_estimated_tokens>1500 -> model-generic-1 for us-west-2.
devin: applied prefill concurrency change across 6 hosts; command returned success.
sre-bot: Deploy event: runtimectl changes propagated to 6 hosts in us-west-2 (ids: h-101..h-106). No failures.
mira: monitoring... p95 dropping to 450ms, p99 to ~1.2s, streaming stalls down 60% vs peak. eviction rate trending down.
sam: client impact summary for CS: ~120 sessions affected by routing rule, degraded quality for those sessions (fallback model), temporary. No data exposure, no 5xx spike.
ashley: good. next ops: create a small follow-up ticket to investigate root cause: why prefill vs decode imbalance happened. assign to eng-runtime and eng-sre. include slab fragmentation traces, allocation patterns, and workload fingerprinting.
devin: logging snapshots saved: /artifacts/kv/1766000001/allocations-*.tar.gz. will attach to the ticket.
ashley: planning a warm restart of one hostpool node to defragment slabs? thoughts?
lia: warm restart can help but do rolling one at a time; coordinate with capacity. Might not be necessary now that pressure is down.
mira: recommend we keep prefill.max_concurrent=2 for next 15min, then gradually increase while watching fragmentation. also add a temporary alert to trigger at fragmentation index >0.3.
ashley: agreed. i'll open the incident handoff note for night oncall: include mitigation steps taken, artifacts location, routing temporary rule id, and follow-up ticket id.
sam: CS notified at 1766000105. running customer outreach for the 5 largest affected orgs.
alex: routing rollback scheduled at 1766000600 unless we extend. I put a changelog entry in infra: CL-45675.
devin: follow-up items: (1) evaluate allocator to reduce fragmentation under mixed prefill/decode workloads, (2) add scoring to route extremely long sessions to pre-warmed caches, (3) consider adaptive prefill concurrency autoscaling.
ashley: thanks everyone. leaving a handoff: if fragmentation index creeps back above 0.25 or p99 > 2s, page oncall. handing to night oncall: @mira -> please pick up and coordinate.
mira: acknowledged, will take it. incident-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 1766000245. Postmortem required.
